question:
In a Young’s double-slit experiment, the slit separation is $d=0.40\,\text{mm}$ and the screen is at a distance $D=1.6\,\text{m}$. Monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda=600\,\text{nm}$ is used, but the source has a finite coherence length $L_c=4.2\,\mu\text{m}$.

A plane-parallel glass slab of thickness $t=6.0\,\mu\text{m}$ and refractive index $\mu=1.50$ is introduced in front of slit $S_1$ only (covering that beam completely).

Take $y$ as the transverse coordinate on the screen measured from the point $O$ (the central bright position when no slab is used), with $y$ positive towards $S_1$. Use the small-angle relation for geometrical path difference:
$$(S_2P-S_1P)\approx \dfrac{d\,y}{D}.$$

Assume that interference fringes are observable only at those points where the magnitude of the net optical path difference satisfies $|\Delta|\le L_c$.

Find (i) the new position $y_0$ of the central bright fringe (order $m=0$) relative to $O$, 

(ii) the total number $N$ of bright fringes that can be observed on the screen.
